clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man presented with bilateral flank pain, dyspnea, urinary frequency, foamy urine, and bilateral floater symptoms. He had a recent diagnosis of anterior uveitis one week prior to hospital admission. Initial laboratory tests revealed acute kidney injury with elevated BUN (26 mg/dL), serum creatinine (2.3 mg/dL), and decreased eGFR (30.9 mL/min). Ophthalmological examination confirmed mild inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber of both eyes. A kidney biopsy showed diffuse interstitial infiltration of lymphocytes and eosinophils, mild tubular atrophy with focal fibrosis, and no evidence of immune complex deposition, consistent with tubulointerstitial nephritis. The temporal association of uveitis preceding the renal symptoms, along with the biopsy findings, supported the diagnosis of TINU syndrome.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms including bilateral flank pain, dyspnea on exertion, urinary frequency, and foamy urine.
Patient was diagnosed with anterior uveitis one week prior to hospital admission for renal symptoms.
Laboratory tests showed elevated BUN (26 mg/dL), serum creatinine (2.3 mg/dL), and decreased eGFR (30.9 mL/min), indicating renal dysfunction.
Slit lamp examination revealed mild inflammatory cells (1+ to 2+) in the anterior chamber of both eyes, confirming uveitis.

Kidney biopsy demonstrated diffuse interstitial infiltration of lymphocytes and eosinophils, mild tubular atrophy with focal fibrosis, and absence of electron-dense deposits or immune complexes, consistent with tubulointerstitial nephritis.
Kidney ultrasonography showed elevated echogenicity of the parenchyma.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Kidney biopsy showed no electron-dense deposits on electron microscopy and no antibody deposits or immune complexes on immunofluorescent studies (E006).

remaining_uncertainties: Specific urinalysis findings (e.g., sterile pyuria, proteinuria, hematuria)
Explicit investigation or ruling out of traditional Korean herbal medicine-induced tubulointerstitial nephritis
